items.title: Red Wings activate Marco Kasper, Mason Appleton off IR
items.desc: Kasper has missed all but one game this season, while Appleton has missed all but two games.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Red Wings have activated Marco Kasper and Mason Appleton off injured reserve. Kasper has missed all but one game this season, while Appleton has missed all but two.

The samples are tiny, so treat these as hints. In his one game, Kasper played 10.83 minutes and the Red Wings controlled 71% of the 5-on-5 chance quality (expected goals, our measure of how good a team's shots are) with him on the ice. Appleton sits at 73% over two games. Detroit as a whole is at 53% at 5-on-5 so far this season, so both skaters pushed play well above the team norm in limited work. The Wings are 7-8-3, and their goals scored trail the quality of their chances by 11.1, so a healthier forward group could help close that gap. Kasper, the eighth pick in 2022, scored 9 goals last season and is worth a look as depth in deeper fantasy leagues once his minutes settle. We'd watch whether either forward moves above the 10-minute mark in the coming games.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Toronto defenseman Morgan Rielly is out day-to-day with a lower-body injury after missing one game, while Colin Sissons was hurt on Sunday night and is out week-to-week.

The Leafs can't afford more losses from the lineup. They sit at 8-9-2 with 18 points through 19 games, and our numbers say the record is not a fluke. TOR has earned 47.1% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality), and that slips to 46% at five-on-five. They are outplaying no one so far this season. What has kept them afloat is finishing: they have scored 6.5 goals more than expected, and their goalies have saved 1.6 more than expected. Both can fade. The special teams are modest too, with the power play creating 0.68 expected goals per game and the penalty kill allowing 0.8. Losing a regular defenseman, even briefly, puts more pressure on a team whose underlying play is already below even and whose results have leaned on above-average finishing.

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Sharks have activated Alex Wennberg off injured reserve, back in the lineup after missing time since October with an upper-body injury.

San Jose needs bodies who can tilt the ice, because right now it tilts the wrong way. The Sharks are 7-11-1 with 42% of the expected goals (the quality of chances each side creates), and they've scored 9.5 fewer goals than those chances usually produce. The one thing holding up is the goaltending, 9.1 goals better than expected. That's a team being outplayed and bailed out at the same time, and goaltending like that rarely lasts a full season. A veteran center doesn't fix a 42% team, but he does push someone out of a role he shouldn't be playing, and that's where we'd look first when Wennberg is back.

items.title: 'He Just Gave Up On Us': Jets' Arniel Talks Hellebuyck Trade, Devils' Decision To Sit Goalie Out
items.desc: Winnipeg Jets head coach Scott Arniel did not shy away when asked to share his thoughts on the New Jersey Devils' decision to sit Connor Hellebuyck ahead of his return to Canada Life Centre.

stories.take:
Scott Arniel isn't pretending the Connor Hellebuyck trade was amicable. Asked by The Hockey News about New Jersey sitting Hellebuyck ahead of his return to Canada Life Centre, the Jets coach's answer made the headline: "He just gave up on us."

That is the story, and it will follow Hellebuyck into Winnipeg whenever he does play there. On the ice, the split so far is less dramatic than the words. In five games for the Devils he's at +1.46 goals saved above expected (saves beyond what the shot quality predicts), good but not carrying anyone, on a 13-5-0 team that takes 59% of the expected goals. Winnipeg is 7-8-3, has 48% of the chances and has scored 7.2 fewer goals than its looks usually produce. The Jets' hole is at the other end of the rink, which probably makes hearing about the goalie harder, not easier.

The data lists Crotty with OTT, so we can't confirm from our numbers which club he was with, and we'd treat that as a question mark until the transaction is clear.

Pitlick is the one we can read. He is pointless in 12 games so far this season, but he has barely played, averaging 7.64 minutes. His shot quality sits about 1.6 goals below what his chances should have produced (1.62 expected, none scored), which looks like bad finishing on a tiny sample rather than a real flaw. At 5-on-5, MIN has had 52.83% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, so he hasn't hurt them. For a MIN team at 12-3-4 with 56.4% of expected goals, sending down a fourth-liner barely shifts anything. Crotty played just 3 games, so there's nothing to learn from his numbers.

items.desc: Some unwanted news for a team already experiencing enough struggles this season. When speaking to the media, Columbus Blue Jackets head coach Rick Bowness announced that forward Conor Garland will not be in the lineup on Tuesday night, when the Blue Jackets…

stories.take:
Daily Faceoff reports Conor Garland is out indefinitely with an upper-body injury, and Rick Bowness said he won't play Tuesday. For a 7-8-0 Columbus team that is already short on scoring, it's one more thing.

Garland's season had been a frustrating one: no goals and one assist in 15 games on 1.56 expected goals (the quality of his chances, added up), so the finish was running about a goal and a half behind the looks. Bad luck was part of it, though not all. The Blue Jackets have taken about 43% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on the ice, roughly six points worse than without him. Columbus sits at 46% overall and is leaning on goaltending that has saved 4.4 more than expected. Going by Bowness's usage, Steven Lorentz is the likeliest to inherit Garland's minutes and second power-play time, but that's our projection, not something we've seen yet.

The Hockey News, citing Sportsnet's Elliotte Friedman, reports that Canadiens prospects Michael Hage and Alexander Zharovsky "will be available" to Montreal at the end of the season. In plain terms: when their current seasons finish, the Canadiens expect to be able to bring them in.

That's a good problem for an 11-3-3 team, but our numbers say the current group needs help more than the standings suggest. Montreal has 49% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) overall. The record leans on goaltending, which has saved 6.6 goals above expected. At five on five the share is a healthier 52%, so this isn't a mirage, but it's not a juggernaut either.

Prospects arriving in the spring rarely change a season. What it does is give Montreal options: in a playoff race, or a deep run, two skilled young forwards are a nice thing to have in reserve if the saves start to run out.

items.title: Rangers, James Reimer Contract Termination Echoes Historically Harsh Reality For Multiple Longtime NHL Goaltenders
items.desc: The New York Rangers have mutually agreed to terminate the contract of goalie James Reimer on Saturday. But while this is likely the end of Reimer's NHL career, his longevity is to be admired. Even the best goalies end their NHL careers in a non-ideal manner.

stories.take:
The Rangers and James Reimer have mutually agreed to terminate his contract, The Hockey News reports, and the outlet frames it as the likely end of his NHL career. It came a day after Daily Faceoff reported he had been placed on waivers.

The end was quiet on the ice too. Reimer appeared in one game this season, in relief, and allowed three goals on eight shots. Last season he played 14 games at 1.67 goals below expected. That is not how anyone in Toronto will remember him. A fourth-round pick of the Leafs in 2006, "Optimus Reim" became a cult favourite there before long stops across the league, and lasting as an NHL goalie for well over a decade is rare. As The Hockey News puts it, even the best goalies rarely get to leave on their own terms.

For New York, nothing changes in net. The Rangers' worry is finishing: 5.66 fewer goals than their chances usually produce.

items.desc: The Buffalo Sabres should have entered this season looking to build upon the momentum from last year. Instead, a summer full of questionable moves and the reported unwillingness to pay up for Connor Hellebuyck has left the franchise with more questions than…

stories.take:
The Hockey News published an opinion piece arguing that Sabres GM Kekalainen's reported unwillingness to pay up for Connor Hellebuyck has proven costly for Buffalo. Hellebuyck now plays for New Jersey, a team that sits in the story only as his current club.

The numbers show a Buffalo team that looks more average than broken. The Sabres are 8-6-3 through 17 games, and their share of expected goals (the quality of chances each side creates) is 50%, an even split. Their goals minus expected goals is -6, so they have scored six fewer than their chances suggest, and their goalies have saved exactly what was expected, a goals saved above expected of 0. That points to a finishing problem more than a goaltending hole. Hellebuyck has a .913 save percentage and 1.46 goals saved above expected in five games so far this season, a small sample. Last year he saved 3.43 goals above expected over 57 games. The case that he would have lifted Buffalo is plausible, but the data doesn't show it as a gap yet.
